curriculum.title: Can Belief in God Be Rational?

core.big_idea: Arguments from existence, order, morality, and consciousness can support theism but should not be represented as coercive proofs.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Wisdom and Worship: Apologetics within the Faith Under Pressure cycle

claims.statement: Scripture presents creation, moral awareness, and human dependence as pointing beyond themselves to God.
Arguments from existence, order, morality, and consciousness can support theism but should not be represented as coercive proofs.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The lesson moves from biblical claims about God and creation to philosophical arguments for theism. Those arguments can supply cumulative rational support, but their formal premises and probability judgments are philosophical reasoning rather than direct biblical propositions.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that arguments from existence, order, morality, and consciousness can support theism but should not be represented as coercive proofs.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The principal passage is Psalm 19; Acts 17:22-31.
Arguments from existence, order, morality, and consciousness can support theism but should not be represented as coercive proofs.
The lesson belongs in Wisdom and Worship.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.
Name one faithful response without claiming more than the passage supports.
become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, or love as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

quiz.question: Which reading habit is most responsible?
options: Observe context and genre before concluding.
Start with the application you want.

answer.text: Observe context and genre before concluding.

quiz.explanation: Observation and context precede synthesis and application.

quiz.question: Arguments from existence, order, morality, and consciousness can support theism but should not be represented as coercive proofs.
